_note: REAL drugs, real quotes, real regulatory outcome. Companion to verdict-eval.json, which uses constructed cases to isolate one rule each. This one asks the opposite question: over packages nobody designed for a test, does the adjudicator flag hepatotoxicity where the label ultimately did?
_groundTruth: GRADED, and read from each drug's own review rather than from memory or an uncited web page. A drug counts as a positive when its review records a LIVER-RELATED REGULATORY ACTION: a boxed warning (turalio) or hepatotoxicity carried into Warnings and Precautions / product labelling (lumakras, krazati, trikafta). Four positives, ten negatives. An earlier version counted only boxed warnings and had ONE positive out of fourteen, which no accuracy figure could survive.
_theImbalance: 10 positives and 10 negatives. The original fixture had 1 usable positive and called the imbalance structural and unfixable, because the only drugs with genuine negative outcomes - troglitazone and tolcapone - are refused by the upload gate. That was true of THOSE two documents and not of the class: six drugs carrying a BOXED warning naming hepatic injury, two of them withdrawn from the US market for it, extract cleanly and are now cases. Sensitivity is therefore a rate here rather than a single observation. Every expectFlag was checked against the label rather than assumed - doing so corrected two intended keys - and only drugs with an unambiguous boxed hepatic warning were added, because almost every modern oncology label carries some hepatic language and a borderline key would mark the model wrong for being right.
_findingsAreNotPreLabelled: Every finding is asserted `ambiguous` and its detail is the verbatim quote with its page. Marking turalio's findings `toxic` would encode the answer in the input and score the model for reading my label back. `ambiguous` is a real value in the schema and means exactly this: here is what the document says, you decide what follows.

rules.name: Human relevance
rules.statement: Human-cell evidence defeats animal in vivo evidence when the question is human hepatotoxicity.

rules.name: Exposure relevance
rules.statement: A finding at an exposure far above the projected human Cmax carries less weight than one at or near it.

rules.name: Reversibility
rules.statement: Damage that reverses on withdrawal is weaker evidence of a safety concern than damage that persists.

_rejectedCandidates: Three candidates were searched and rejected, and orgovyx is why every hit had to be read rather than counted: its only hepatotoxicity sentences are about BICALUTAMIDE, a comparator drug named in the review, plus a generic reference to FDA DILI monitoring guidance. A regex that counted hits would have labelled relugolix hepatotoxic on another drug's evidence.
